info: Opening track of Ultimate Love Forever, a seven-song album and the Sub Pop debut of New York songwriter Lex Walton. The album was produced by Walton and Dan Boeckner of Wolf Parade and Handsome Furs, and recorded, mixed and mastered by Ben Greenberg. The track runs about two minutes.
flags: Digital release date Aug. 26 comes from Audiomack and a FEMMUSIC post dated that day; Sub Pop pages seen only say the album is out now. Color vinyl LP and CD follow Nov. 20, 2026.

info: Heavens to Betsy, the Olympia, Washington duo of Corin Tucker and Tracy Sawyer, recorded this song on a demo in February 1992, engineered by Molly Neuman of Bratmobile. It is track 7 and the title of a 16-track collection that also gathers the 1993 These Monsters Are Real and 1994 Direction recordings. It is their first release since Calculated (1994).
flags: Label is Kill Rock Stars, not Yoyo Recordings as in the plan (Yoyo was the Olympia studio/label for the band's earlier comp appearances). Press calls the 1992 demo never-before-heard, but a Discogs listing shows a 1992 demo cassette with this song, so the song's true first appearance is arguably the 1992 demo cassette.

info: Track 6 of 12 on Blame the Clown, the second full-length from the New Orleans duo of Caspian Hollywell and RJ. Melrose Billiard is credited with lead guitar on this song. The album is released on Chain Smoking Records.
flags: Dates conflict: Bandcamp says Feb. 13, 2026, Turbo Discos Bandcamp says Feb. 17, 2026, and Rate Your Music lists Sept. 2025. Possible earlier digital or other-label release; verify. Sources also differ on the second member's surname (Ramone vs Santos), so only first name used.

track: Top Of The World Hwy No. 2
info: Track 6 on Florida Water Blues, the New Orleans duo's 2026 album, sequenced right after Guided Thunder. The song runs about two minutes. Reviewers compare it to a barroom blues band discovering Iggy Pop.
flags: Release label not confirmed in sources seen (Bandcamp, Goner, Thrillhouse and a Sub Pop store listing all carry it); plan says Chain Smoking Records.

parent_release: You're Gonna Need a Little Music (Republic Records), July 17, 2026
info: Second single from the Leeds band's third studio album, following the lead single Redeemer, and track 2 on the record. The album was produced by Justin Meldal-Johnsen. Yard Act's 2022 debut, The Overload, was nominated for the Mercury Prize.
flags: Label listed inconsistently (Republic per Stereogum and Republic store; Island per some UK outlets). DIY Magazine gave July 13 for the album; most sources say July 17.

info: Lead single and opening track from the debut album by the Manchester four-piece, produced by Loren Humphrey and recorded at Greenmount Studios in Leeds. The band used a live recording of the Velvet Underground's What Goes On as a reference point. The video was made with FC United of Manchester.
flags: Album date Aug. 21, 2026 is well sourced. The May 20 single date rests on Spotify metadata and a May 21 blog post; no press release seen.

parent_release: do you love the color of the sky? (Polyvinyl Record Co.), Oct. 16, 2026
info: Lead single from the Los Angeles band's first album for Polyvinyl, the follow-up to 2024's Free Energy. The album was produced by the band with Joo-Joo Ashworth and mastered by Mikey Young. Emma Maatman sings lead.
flags: Sources disagree on whether this is the band's third or fourth album, so no count given.

info: Lead single and opening track on Gravity Freeze, the band's sixth studio album and first under the Little Barrie name since drummer Virgil Howe died in 2017. Barrie Cadogan wrote it on bass, and the album was co-produced by Rupert Lyddon at Rat Salad Studios in London.
flags: Single date inferred from a Feb. 26 audio upload and a Feb. 27 Song of the Day post; verify exact day. Album date May 22, 2026 is well sourced.

info: Lead single from the duo's fifth studio album, Dead Company, released alongside the album announcement. It is their first new music since Back to the Water Below (2023). A second single, the title track Dead Company, followed on Oct. 6.
flags: Album date moved: August coverage said Nov. 13, while Wikipedia, the band store and October coverage say Nov. 6, 2026. Used Nov. 6. Label is Warner Records.

track: My Girlfriend is a Rock (Radio Edit)
parent_release: Politics EP (Wild Child Records); reissued by Get Hip Recordings, Feb. 5, 2021
info: From the Politics EP, the debut record by the Dallas punk band, issued on Wild Child Records, the label run by manager Tom Ordon. The four-song EP also has Politics, My Life Is Ruined and I Can't Help You. The song was a regional hit in San Francisco, Sacramento and Boston and was later covered by the Angry Samoans and Wool.
flags: July 1978 comes from a Twangsville Revisited blog post; Wikipedia says only 'later in 1978' and Discogs says 1978. One blog calls the EP self-released, but Wild Child is the label per Wikipedia-derived and Dallas Observer coverage. Date and Get Hip date are for the original song and reissue; radio edit has no separate release.

parent_release: Fun, Fun, Fun... EP (Moment Productions), reissued by 540 Records, 2013
info: Title track of the 1982 EP by the Austin band, formed in 1977 with Randy 'Biscuit' Turner on vocals, Tim Kerr on guitar and Chris Gates on bass. The EP was produced by Spot. Austin's Fun Fun Fun Fest took its name from the record.
flags: Exact day not found. An Austin Chronicle review calls it 1981's Fun Fun Fun; Wikipedia, Discogs and Rate Your Music say 1982. Label credited as Moment Productions (plan says Moment Records).

parent_release: The Greatest Gift (Touch and Go Records, compilation), 1991
info: From the Austin band's 1984 self-titled EP on Rabid Cat, recorded in July 1984 at Earth and Sky Studio. The lineup was David Yow on vocals, Brett Bradford on guitar, David Wm. Sims on bass and Rey Washam on drums. The EP is the first eight tracks of the 1991 Touch and Go compilation The Greatest Gift, and Yow later fronted the Jesus Lizard.
flags: Exact day not found. EP label is Rabid Cat (cat. no. RAB-004-SA), vinyl only. Track list conflict: a Grokipedia page lists Greatest Gift on the EP while the Wikipedia snippet cited a different title; Discogs lists the 1991 compilation's tracks 1-8 as the EP, so confirm Greatest Gift is on it.

info: Lead single from Electriclarryland, the San Antonio band's seventh studio album. It reached number one on the Billboard Modern Rock Tracks chart and was the top-ranked song of 1996 on that listing. The album reached number 31 on the Billboard 200 and was certified gold on Aug. 20, 1996.
flags: April 11, 1996 is the date the song was sent to alternative and college radio (Wikipedia, citing Billboard); commercial single formats were also issued in 1996. Songfacts says it was not sold as a single in the US; Wikipedia lists a US CD single. Songwriting credits not confirmed so omitted.

info: Track 5 on Goat, the band's second studio album, produced by Steve Albini and released on Touch and Go. Singer David Yow had previously fronted Scratch Acid. Goat was remastered by Albini and Bob Weston and reissued in 2009 with five bonus tracks.
flags: The March 15 day comes from a single blog/Discogs-based source; other sources say only March 1991. Verify the day.
